Blow-up criteria for Boussinesq system and MHD system and Landau-Lifshitz equations in a bounded domain

Jishan Fan Affiliation: Department of Applied Mathematics, Affiliation: Nanjing Forestry University, Nanjing 210037, P.R.China Affiliation: E-mail: fanjishan@njfu.edu.cn Affiliation: Wenjun Sun,    Junping Yin ††thanks: Corresponding author. Affiliation: Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics, Affiliation: Beijing, 100088, P.R.China Affiliation: E-mail: sun_wenjun@iapcm.ac.cn,    yinjp829829@126.com
Abstract

In this paper, we prove some blow-up criteria for the 3D Boussinesq system with zero heat conductivity and MHD system and Landau-Lifshitz equations in a bounded domain.
Keywords : blow-up criterion, Boussinesq system, MHD system, Landau-Lifshitz equations.
Mathematics subject classifications (2010): 35Q30, 76D03, 76D09.
Running Title: Boussinesq-MHD-Landau-Lifshitz

1 Introduction

Let Ω\Omega be a bounded, simply connected domain in ℝ3\mathbb{R}^{3} with smooth boundary ∂Ω\partial\Omega, and ν\nu be the unit outward normal vector to ∂Ω\partial\Omega. First, we consider the regularity criterion of the Boussinesq system with zero heat conductivity:

div​u=0,\displaystyle\mathrm{div}\,u=0, (1.1)
∂tu+u⋅∇u+∇π−Δ​u=θ​e3,\displaystyle\partial_{t}u+u\cdot\nabla u+\nabla\pi-\Delta u=\theta e_{3}, (1.2)
∂tθ+u⋅∇θ=0inΩ×(0,∞),\displaystyle\partial_{t}\theta+u\cdot\nabla\theta=0\ \ \mathrm{in}\ \ \Omega\times(0,\infty), (1.3)
u⋅ν=0,curlu×ν=0on∂Ω×(0,∞),\displaystyle u\cdot\nu=0,\mathrm{curl}\,u\times\nu=0\ \ \mathrm{on}\ \ \partial\Omega\times(0,\infty), (1.4)
(u,θ)​(⋅,0)=(u0,θ0)inΩ⊆ℝ3,\displaystyle(u,\theta)(\cdot,0)=(u_{0},\theta_{0})\ \ \mathrm{in}\ \ \Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{3}, (1.5)

where u,πu,\pi, and θ\theta denote unknown velocity vector field, pressure scalar, and temperature scalar of the fluid, respectively. ω:=curl​u\omega:=\mathrm{curl}\,u is the vorticity and e3:=(0,0,1)te_{3}:=(0,0,1)^{t}.

When θ=0\theta=0, (1.1) and (1.2) are the well-known Navier-Stokes system. Giga [1], Kim [2], Kang and Kim [3] have proved some Serrin type regularity criteria.

The first aim of this paper is to prove a new regularity criterion for the problem (1.1)-(1.5), we will prove

Theorem 1.1.

Let u0∈H3,θ0∈W1,pu_{0}\in H^{3},\theta_{0}\in W^{1,p} with 3<p≤63<p\leq 6 and div​u0=0\mathrm{div}\,u_{0}=0 in Ω\Omega and u0⋅ν=0,curl​u0×ν=0u_{0}\cdot\nu=0,\mathrm{curl}\,u_{0}\times\nu=0 on ∂Ω\partial\Omega. Let (u,θ)(u,\theta) be a strong solution of the problem (1.1)-(1.5). If uu satisfies

∇u∈L1​(0,T,B​M​O​(Ω))\nabla u\in L^{1}(0,T;BMO(\Omega)) (1.6)

with 0<T<∞0<T<\infty, then the solution (u,θ)(u,\theta) can be extended beyond T>0T>0. Here B​M​OBMO denotes the space of bounded mean oscillation.

Secondly, we consider the blow-up criterion of the 3D MHD system

div​u=div​b=0,\displaystyle\mathrm{div}\,u=\mathrm{div}\,b=0, (1.7)
∂tu+u⋅∇u+∇(π+12​|b|2)−Δ​u=b⋅∇b,\displaystyle\partial_{t}u+u\cdot\nabla u+\nabla\left(\pi+\frac{1}{2}|b|^{2}\right)-\Delta u=b\cdot\nabla b, (1.8)
∂tb+u⋅∇b−b⋅∇u=Δ​bi​nΩ×(0,∞),\displaystyle\partial_{t}b+u\cdot\nabla b-b\cdot\nabla u=\Delta b\ \ in\ \ \Omega\times(0,\infty), (1.9)
u⋅ν=0,curlu×ν=0,b⋅ν=0,curlb×ν=0on∂Ω×(0,∞),\displaystyle u\cdot\nu=0,\mathrm{curl}\,u\times\nu=0,b\cdot\nu=0,\mathrm{curl}\,b\times\nu=0\ \ on\ \ \partial\Omega\times(0,\infty), (1.10)
(u,b)​(⋅,0)=(u0,b0)i​nΩ⊆ℝ3.\displaystyle(u,b)(\cdot,0)=(u_{0},b_{0})\ \ in\ \ \Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{3}. (1.11)

Here bb is the magnetic field of the fluid.

It is well-known that the problem (1.7)-(1.11) has a unique local strong solution [4]. But whether this local solution can exist globally is an outstanding problem. Kang and Kim [3] prove some Serrin type regularity criteria.

The second aim of this paper is to prove a new regularity criterion for the problem (1.7)-(1.11), we will prove

Theorem 1.2.

Let u0,b0∈H3u_{0},b_{0}\in H^{3} with div​u0=div​b0=0\mathrm{div}\,u_{0}=\mathrm{div}\,b_{0}=0 in Ω\Omega and u0⋅ν=b0⋅ν=0,curl​u0×ν=curl​b0×ν=0u_{0}\cdot\nu=b_{0}\cdot\nu=0,\mathrm{curl}\,u_{0}\times\nu=\mathrm{curl}\,b_{0}\times\nu=0 on ∂Ω\partial\Omega. Let (u,b)(u,b) be a strong solution to the problem (1.7)-(1.11). If (1.6) holds true, then the solution (u,b)(u,b) can be extended beyond T>0T>0.

Remark 1.1.

When Ω:=ℝ3\Omega:=\mathbb{R}^{3}, our result gives the following well-known regularity criterion

ω:=curl​u∈L1​(0,T,B˙∞,∞0),\omega:=\mathrm{curl}\,u\in L^{1}(0,T;\dot{B}_{\infty,\infty}^{0}),

but the method of proof we used is different from that in [14, 15]. Here B˙∞,∞0\dot{B}_{\infty,\infty}^{0} denotes the homogeneous Besov space [13].

Next, we consider the following 3D density-dependent MHD equations:

div​u=div​b=0,\displaystyle\mathrm{div}\,u=\mathrm{div}\,b=0, (1.12)
∂tρ+div⁡(ρ​u)=0,\displaystyle\partial_{t}\rho+\mathrm{div}\,(\rho u)=0, (1.13)
∂t(ρ​u)+div⁡(ρ​u⊗u)+∇(π+12​|b|2)−Δ​u=b⋅∇b,\displaystyle\partial_{t}(\rho u)+\mathrm{div}\,(\rho u\otimes u)+\nabla\left(\pi+\frac{1}{2}|b|^{2}\right)-\Delta u=b\cdot\nabla b, (1.14)
∂tb+u⋅∇b−b⋅∇u=Δ​bi​nΩ×(0,∞),\displaystyle\partial_{t}b+u\cdot\nabla b-b\cdot\nabla u=\Delta b\ \ in\ \ \Omega\times(0,\infty), (1.15)
u=0,b⋅ν=0,curlb×ν=0on∂Ω×(0,∞),\displaystyle u=0,b\cdot\nu=0,\mathrm{curl}\,b\times\nu=0\ \ on\ \ \partial\Omega\times(0,\infty), (1.16)
(ρ,ρ​u,b)​(⋅,0)=(ρ0,ρ0​u0,b0)i​nΩ⊂ℝ3.\displaystyle(\rho,\rho u,b)(\cdot,0)=(\rho_{0},\rho_{0}u_{0},b_{0})\ \ in\ \ \Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{3}. (1.17)

For this problem, in [5], Wu proved that if the initial data ρ0,u0\rho_{0},u_{0}, and b0b_{0} satisfy

0≤ρ0∈H2,u0∈H01∩H2,b0∈H2,−Δ​u0+∇(π0+12​|b0|2)=b0⋅∇b0+ρ0​g0\leq\rho_{0}\in H^{2},u_{0}\in H_{0}^{1}\cap H^{2},b_{0}\in H^{2},-\Delta u_{0}+\nabla\left(\pi_{0}+\frac{1}{2}|b_{0}|^{2}\right)=b_{0}\cdot\nabla b_{0}+\sqrt{\rho_{0}}g (1.18)

for some (π0,g)∈H1×L2(\pi_{0},g)\in H^{1}\times L^{2}, then there exists a positive time T∗T_{*} and a unique strong solution (ρ,u,b)(\rho,u,b) to the problem (1.12)-(1.17) such that

ρ∈C([0,T∗];H2),u∈C([0,T∗];H01∩H2)∩L2(0,T∗;H2),ut∈L2(0,T∗;H01),ρut∈L∞(0,T∗;L2),b∈L∞(0,T∗;H2)∩L2(0,T∗;H3),bt∈L∞(0,T∗;L2)∩L2(0,T∗;H1).\begin{array}[]{l}\rho\in C([0,T_{*}];H^{2}),u\in C([0,T_{*}];H_{0}^{1}\cap H^{2})\cap L^{2}(0,T_{*};H^{2}),\\ u_{t}\in L^{2}(0,T_{*};H_{0}^{1}),\sqrt{\rho}u_{t}\in L^{\infty}(0,T_{*};L^{2}),\\ b\in L^{\infty}(0,T_{*};H^{2})\cap L^{2}(0,T_{*};H^{3}),b_{t}\in L^{\infty}(0,T_{*};L^{2})\cap L^{2}(0,T_{*};H^{1}).\end{array} (1.19)

And when b=0b=0, Kim [2] proved the following regularity criterion:

u∈L2​ss−3​(0,T,Lws​(Ω))with​ 3<s≤∞.u\in L^{\frac{2s}{s-3}}(0,T;L_{w}^{s}(\Omega))\ \ \mathrm{with}\ \ 3<s\leq\infty. (1.20)

Here LwsL_{w}^{s} denotes the weak-LsL^{s} space and Lw∞=L∞L_{w}^{\infty}=L^{\infty}.

The aim of this paper is to refine (1.20), we will prove

Theorem 1.3.

Let ρ0,u0\rho_{0},u_{0}, and b0b_{0} satisfy (1.18). Let (ρ,u,b)(\rho,u,b) be a strong solution of the problem (1.12)-(1.17) in the class (1.19). If uu satisfies one of the following two conditions:

(i)∫0T‖u⁡(t)‖Lws2​ss−31+log⁡(e+‖u⁡(t)‖Lws)​𝑑t<∞w​i​t​h​ 3<s≤∞,\displaystyle(i)\quad\int_{0}^{T}\frac{\|u(t)\|_{L_{w}^{s}}^{\frac{2s}{s-3}}}{1+\log(e+\|u(t)\|_{L_{w}^{s}})}dt<\infty\ \ with\ \ 3<s\leq\infty, (1.21)
(i​i)u∈L2​(0,T,B​M​O​(Ω))\displaystyle(ii)\quad u\in L^{2}(0,T;BMO(\Omega)) (1.22)

with 0<T<∞0<T<\infty, then the solution (ρ,u,b)(\rho,u,b) can be extended beyond T>0T>0.

Finally, we consider the 3D Landau-Lifshitz system:

∂td−Δd=d|∇d|2+d×Δd,|d|=1inΩ×(0,∞),\displaystyle\partial_{t}d-\Delta d=d|\nabla d|^{2}+d\times\Delta d,|d|=1\ \ in\ \ \Omega\times(0,\infty), (1.23)
∂νd=0o​n∂Ω×(0,∞),\displaystyle\partial_{\nu}d=0\ \ on\ \ \partial\Omega\times(0,\infty), (1.24)
d(⋅,0)=d0,|d0|=1inΩ⊆ℝ3.\displaystyle d(\cdot,0)=d_{0},|d_{0}|=1\ \ in\ \ \Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{3}. (1.25)

Carbou and Fabrie [6] showed the existence and uniqueness of local smooth solutions. When Ω:=ℝn​(n=2,3,4)\Omega:=\mathbb{R}^{n}\ (n=2,3,4), Fan and Ozawa [7] proved some regularity criteria. The aim of this paper is to prove a logarithmic blow-up criterion for the problem (1.23)-(1.25) when Ω\Omega is a bounded domain. We will prove

Theorem 1.4.

Let d0∈H3​(Ω)d_{0}\in H^{3}(\Omega) with |d0|=1|d_{0}|=1 in Ω\Omega and ∂νd0=0\partial_{\nu}d_{0}=0 on ∂Ω\partial\Omega. Let dd be a local smooth solution to the problem (1.23)-(1.25). If dd satisfies

∫0T‖∇d‖Lq2​qq−31+log⁡(e+‖∇d‖Lq)​𝑑t<∞w​i​t​h​ 3<q≤∞,\int_{0}^{T}\frac{\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}^{\frac{2q}{q-3}}}{1+\log(e+\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}})}dt<\infty\ \ with\ \ 3<q\leq\infty, (1.26)

and 0<T<∞0<T<\infty, then the solution can be extended beyond T>0T>0.

In the following section 2, we give some preliminary Lemmas which will be used in the following sections. The proof of Theorem 1.1 of problem (1.1) -(1.5) will be given in section 3. The new regularly criterion of Theorem 1.2 for the 3D MHD problem (1.7) -(1.11) will be proved in section 4. In section 5 is the proof of the Theorem 1.3, and in the next section 6 we give the main proof of final Theorem 1.4.

2 Preliminary Lemmas

In the following proofs, we will use the following logarithmic Sobolev inequality [8]:

‖∇u‖L∞≤C⁡(1+‖∇u‖B​M​O​log⁡(e+‖u‖Ws,p))withs>1+3p.\|\nabla u\|_{L^{\infty}}\leq C(1+\|\nabla u\|_{BMO}\log(e+\|u\|_{W^{s,p}}))\ \ \mathrm{with}\ \ s>1+\frac{3}{p}. (2.1)

and the following three lemmas.

Lemma 2.1.

([9]). Let Ω⊆ℝ3\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{3} be a smooth bounded domain, let b:Ω→ℝ3b:\Omega\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{3} be a smooth vector field, and let 1<p<∞1<p<\infty. Then

−∫ΩΔb⋅b|b|p−2dx=12∫Ω|b|p−2|∇b|2dx+4p−2p2∫Ω|∇|b|p2|2dx\displaystyle-\int_{\Omega}\Delta b\cdot b|b|^{p-2}dx=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}|b|^{p-2}|\nabla b|^{2}dx+4\frac{p-2}{p^{2}}\int_{\Omega}|\nabla|b|^{\frac{p}{2}}|^{2}dx
−∫∂Ω|b|p−2(b⋅∇)b⋅νdσ−∫∂Ω|b|p−2(curlb×ν)⋅bdσ.\displaystyle\qquad-\int_{\partial\Omega}|b|^{p-2}(b\cdot\nabla)b\cdot\nu d\sigma-\int_{\partial\Omega}|b|^{p-2}(\mathrm{curl}\,b\times\nu)\cdot bd\sigma. (2.2)
Lemma 2.2.

([10, 11]). Let Ω\Omega be a smooth and bounded open set and let 1<p<∞1<p<\infty. Then the following estimate:

‖b‖Lp​(∂Ω)≤C​‖b‖Lp​(Ω)1−1p​‖b‖W1,p​(Ω)1p\|b\|_{L^{p}(\partial\Omega)}\leq C\|b\|_{L^{p}(\Omega)}^{1-\frac{1}{p}}\|b\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}^{\frac{1}{p}} (2.3)

holds for any b∈W1,p​(Ω)b\in W^{1,p}(\Omega).

Lemma 2.3.

There holds

‖f‖L∞​(Ω)≤C⁡(1+‖f‖B​M​O​(Ω)​log12⁡(e+‖f‖W1,4​(Ω)))\|f\|_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}\leq C(1+\|f\|_{BMO(\Omega)}\log^{\frac{1}{2}}(e+\|f\|_{W^{1,4}(\Omega)})) (2.4)

for any f∈W01,4​(Ω)f\in W_{0}^{1,4}(\Omega).

Proof. When Ω:=ℝ3\Omega:=\mathbb{R}^{3}, (2.4) has been proved in Ogawa [12]. When Ω\Omega is a bounded domain in ℝ3\mathbb{R}^{3}. We can define

f~:={fi​nΩ,0i​nΩc:=ℝ3∖Ω.\tilde{f}:=\left\{\begin{array}[]{lcl}f&\quad in&\Omega,\\ 0&\quad in&\Omega^{c}:=\mathbb{R}^{3}\setminus\Omega.\end{array}\right.

Then we have [10, Page 71]

‖f~‖W1,4​(ℝ3)=‖f‖W1,4​(Ω)\|\tilde{f}\|_{W^{1,4}(\mathbb{R}^{3})}=\|f\|_{W^{1,4}(\Omega)}

and it is obvious that

‖f~‖L∞​(ℝ3)=‖f‖L∞​(Ω),‖f~‖B​M​O​(ℝ3)=‖f‖B​M​O​(Ω).\|\tilde{f}\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{3})}=\|f\|_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)},\|\tilde{f}\|_{BMO(\mathbb{R}^{3})}=\|f\|_{BMO(\Omega)}.

Thus (2.4) is proved.

□\square

Finally, when bb satisfies b⋅ν=0b\cdot\nu=0 on ∂Ω\partial\Omega, we will also use the identity

(b⋅∇)b⋅ν=−(b⋅∇)ν⋅bon∂Ω(b\cdot\nabla)b\cdot\nu=-(b\cdot\nabla)\nu\cdot b\ \ \mathrm{on}\ \ \partial\Omega (2.5)

for any sufficiently smooth vector field bb.

3 Proof of Theorem 1.1

This section is devoted to the proof of Theorem 1.1. Since it is easy to prove that the problem (1.1) -(1.5) has a unique local-in-time strong solution, we omit the details here. We only need to establish a priori estimates.

First, thanks to the maximum principle, it follows from (1.1) and (1.3) that

‖θ‖L∞​(0,T,L∞)≤C.\|\theta\|_{L^{\infty}(0,T;L^{\infty})}\leq C. (3.1)

Testing (1.2) by uu and using (1.1) and (3.1), we see that

12​dd​t​∫Ωu2​𝑑x+∫Ω|curl​u|2​𝑑x≤∫Ωθ​e3⋅u​𝑑x≤12​∫Ωθ2​𝑑x+12​∫Ωu2​𝑑x,\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}u^{2}dx+\int_{\Omega}|\mathrm{curl}\,u|^{2}dx\leq\int_{\Omega}\theta e_{3}\cdot udx\leq\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}\theta^{2}dx+\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}u^{2}dx,

which gives

‖u‖L∞​(0,T,L2)+‖u‖L2​(0,T,H1)≤C.\|u\|_{L^{\infty}(0,T;L^{2})}+\|u\|_{L^{2}(0,T;H^{1})}\leq C. (3.2)

Applying curl\mathrm{curl}\, to (1.2) and setting ω:=curl​u\omega:=\mathrm{curl}\,u, we find that

∂tω+u⋅∇ω−Δ​ω=ω⋅∇u+curl⁡(θ​e3).\partial_{t}\omega+u\cdot\nabla\omega-\Delta\omega=\omega\cdot\nabla u+\mathrm{curl}\,(\theta e_{3}). (3.3)

Testing (3.3) by ω\omega and using (1.1) and (3.1), we infer that

12​dd​t​∫Ω|ω|2​𝑑x+∫Ω|curl​ω|2​𝑑x\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}|\omega|^{2}dx+\int_{\Omega}|\mathrm{curl}\,\omega|^{2}dx =\displaystyle= ∫Ω(ω⋅∇)u⋅ωdx+∫Ωθe3curlωdx\displaystyle\int_{\Omega}(\omega\cdot\nabla)u\cdot\omega dx+\int_{\Omega}\theta e_{3}\mathrm{curl}\,\omega dx
≤\displaystyle\leq ‖∇u‖L∞​∫Ωω2​𝑑x+12​∫Ω|curl​ω|2​𝑑x+C,\displaystyle\|\nabla u\|_{L^{\infty}}\int_{\Omega}\omega^{2}dx+\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}|\mathrm{curl}\,\omega|^{2}dx+C,

which implies

dd​t​∫Ω|ω|2​𝑑x+∫Ω|curl​ω|2​𝑑x\displaystyle\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}|\omega|^{2}dx+\int_{\Omega}|\mathrm{curl}\,\omega|^{2}dx ≤\displaystyle\leq C​‖∇u‖L∞​∫Ω|ω|2​𝑑x+C\displaystyle C\|\nabla u\|_{L^{\infty}}\int_{\Omega}|\omega|^{2}dx+C
≤\displaystyle\leq C⁡(1+‖∇u‖B​M​O)​log⁡(e+‖u‖H3)​∫Ω|ω|2​𝑑x+C,\displaystyle C(1+\|\nabla u\|_{BMO})\log(e+\|u\|_{H^{3}})\int_{\Omega}|\omega|^{2}dx+C,

and therefore

∫Ω|ω|2​𝑑x+∫t0t‖curl​ω‖L22​𝑑τ≤C​(e+y)C0​ϵ\int_{\Omega}|\omega|^{2}dx+\int_{t_{0}}^{t}\|\mathrm{curl}\,\omega\|_{L^{2}}^{2}d\tau\leq C(e+y)^{C_{0}\epsilon} (3.4)

provided that

∫t0t‖∇u‖B​M​O​𝑑τ≤ϵ<<1\int_{t_{0}}^{t}\|\nabla u\|_{BMO}d\tau\leq\epsilon<<1 (3.5)

and y⁡(t):=sup[t0,t]‖u‖H3y(t):=\sup\limits_{[t_{0},t]}\|u\|_{H^{3}} for any 0<t0≤t≤T0<t_{0}\leq t\leq T and C0C_{0} is an absolute constant.

Applying ∂t\partial_{t} to (1.2), we deduce that

≤\displaystyle\leq C​‖∂tu+u⋅∇u−θ​e3‖L2\displaystyle C\|\partial_{t}u+u\cdot\nabla u-\theta e_{3}\|_{L^{2}}
≤\displaystyle\leq C​‖ut‖L2+C​‖u‖L6​‖∇u‖L3+C​‖θ‖L2\displaystyle C\|u_{t}\|_{L^{2}}+C\|u\|_{L^{6}}\|\nabla u\|_{L^{3}}+C\|\theta\|_{L^{2}}
≤\displaystyle\leq C​‖ut‖L2+C​‖∇u‖L232​‖u‖H212+C,\displaystyle C\|u_{t}\|_{L^{2}}+C\|\nabla u\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{3}{2}}\|u\|_{H^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}+C,

which implies

‖u‖H2≤C​‖ut‖L2+C​‖∇u‖L23+C≤C​(e+y)C0​ϵ.\|u\|_{H^{2}}\leq C\|u_{t}\|_{L^{2}}+C\|\nabla u\|_{L^{2}}^{3}+C\leq C(e+y)^{C_{0}\epsilon}. (3.8)

Applying ∇\nabla to (1.3), testing by |∇θ|p−2∇θ(2≤p<∞)|\nabla\theta|^{p-2}\nabla\theta\ (2\leq p<\infty) and using (1.1), we get

dd​t​‖∇θ‖Lp\displaystyle\frac{d}{dt}\|\nabla\theta\|_{L^{p}} ≤\displaystyle\leq C​‖∇u‖L∞​‖∇θ‖Lp\displaystyle C\|\nabla u\|_{L^{\infty}}\|\nabla\theta\|_{L^{p}}

5 Proof of Theorem 1.3

This section is devoted to the proof of Theorem 1.3, we only need to establish a priori estimates.

First, it follows from (1.12) and (1.13) that

‖ρ‖L∞​(0,T,L∞)≤C.\|\rho\|_{L^{\infty}(0,T;L^{\infty})}\leq C. (5.1)

Testing (1.14) by uu and using (1.12) and (1.13), we see that

12dd​t∫Ωρu2dx+∫Ω|∇u|2dx=∫Ω(b⋅∇)b⋅udx.\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}\rho u^{2}dx+\int_{\Omega}|\nabla u|^{2}dx=\int_{\Omega}(b\cdot\nabla)b\cdot udx. (5.2)

And testing (1.15) by bb and using (1.12) and (1.16), we find that

12dd​t∫Ω|b|2dx+∫Ω|curlb|2dx=∫Ω(b⋅∇)u⋅bdx.\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}|b|^{2}dx+\int_{\Omega}|\mathrm{curl}\,b|^{2}dx=\int_{\Omega}(b\cdot\nabla)u\cdot bdx. (5.3)

12​dd​t​∫Ω(ρ​|u|2+|b|2)​𝑑x+∫Ω(|∇u|2+|curl​b|2)​𝑑x≤0.\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}(\rho|u|^{2}+|b|^{2})dx+\int_{\Omega}(|\nabla u|^{2}+|\mathrm{curl}\,b|^{2})dx\leq 0. (5.4)

≤\displaystyle\leq C​‖ρ​ut‖L2+C​‖u‖L6​‖∇u‖L212​‖u‖H212+C​‖b‖L6​‖∇b‖L212​‖b‖H212,\displaystyle C\|\sqrt{\rho}u_{t}\|_{L^{2}}+C\|u\|_{L^{6}}\|\nabla u\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\|u\|_{H^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}+C\|b\|_{L^{6}}\|\nabla b\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\|b\|_{H^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}},

which leads to

‖u‖H22≤C​‖ρ​ut‖L22+C​‖∇u‖L26+C​‖∇b‖L26+12​‖b‖H22.\|u\|_{H^{2}}^{2}\leq C\|\sqrt{\rho}u_{t}\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+C\|\nabla u\|_{L^{2}}^{6}+C\|\nabla b\|_{L^{2}}^{6}+\frac{1}{2}\|b\|_{H^{2}}^{2}. (5.21)

Similarly, we have

‖b‖H2\displaystyle\|b\|_{H^{2}} ≤\displaystyle\leq C​‖bt+u⋅∇b−b⋅∇u‖L2\displaystyle C\|b_{t}+u\cdot\nabla b-b\cdot\nabla u\|_{L^{2}}
≤\displaystyle\leq C​‖bt‖L2+C​‖u‖L6​‖∇b‖L3+C​‖b‖L6​‖∇u‖L3\displaystyle C\|b_{t}\|_{L^{2}}+C\|u\|_{L^{6}}\|\nabla b\|_{L^{3}}+C\|b\|_{L^{6}}\|\nabla u\|_{L^{3}}
≤\displaystyle\leq C​‖bt‖L2+C​‖u‖L6​‖∇b‖L212​‖b‖H212+C​‖b‖L6​‖∇u‖L212​‖u‖H212,\displaystyle C\|b_{t}\|_{L^{2}}+C\|u\|_{L^{6}}\|\nabla b\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\|b\|_{H^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}+C\|b\|_{L^{6}}\|\nabla u\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\|u\|_{H^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}},

which implies

‖b‖H22≤C​‖bt‖L22+C​‖∇u‖L26+C​‖∇b‖L26+12​‖u‖H22.\|b\|_{H^{2}}^{2}\leq C\|b_{t}\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+C\|\nabla u\|_{L^{2}}^{6}+C\|\nabla b\|_{L^{2}}^{6}+\frac{1}{2}\|u\|_{H^{2}}^{2}. (5.22)

Combining (5.21) and (5.22), using (5.20) and (5.16), we conclude that

‖u‖H22+‖b‖H22≤C​(e+y)C0​ϵ,\|u\|_{H^{2}}^{2}+\|b\|_{H^{2}}^{2}\leq C(e+y)^{C_{0}\epsilon}, (5.23)

and thus

‖u‖L∞​(0,T,H2)+‖b‖L∞​(0,T,H2)≤C.\|u\|_{L^{\infty}(0,T;H^{2})}+\|b\|_{L^{\infty}(0,T;H^{2})}\leq C. (5.24)

Now it is standard to prove that

‖u‖L2​(0,T,H3)+‖b‖L2​(0,T,H3)≤C,\displaystyle\|u\|_{L^{2}(0,T;H^{3})}+\|b\|_{L^{2}(0,T;H^{3})}\leq C, (5.25)
‖ρ‖L∞​(0,T,H2)≤C.\displaystyle\|\rho\|_{L^{\infty}(0,T;H^{2})}\leq C. (5.26)

(II) Let (1.22) hold true.

Similarly to (5.7), we take s=∞s=\infty and using (2.4), we still get (5.7) provided that

∫t0T‖u⁡(t)‖B​M​O2​𝑑t≤ϵ<<1.\int_{t_{0}}^{T}\|u(t)\|_{BMO}^{2}dt\leq\epsilon<<1. (5.27)

We still have (5.9), (5.10), (5.11) with s=∞s=\infty, (5.12) with s=∞s=\infty, (5.13) with s=∞s=\infty, (5.14), (5.15) with s=∞s=\infty, and then using (5.27) and (2.4), we arrive at (5.16) and (5.17). Then by the same calculations as that in (5.18)-(5.26), we conclude that (5.18)-(5.26) hold true.

This completes the proof of Theorem 1.3.

□\square

6 Proof of Theorem 1.4

This section is devoted to the proof of Theorem 1.4, we only need to establish a priori estimates.

First, using the formula a×(b×c)=(a⋅c)​b−(a⋅b)​ca\times(b\times c)=(a\cdot c)b-(a\cdot b)c, and the fact that |d|=1|d|=1 implies d​Δ​d=−|∇d|2d\Delta d=-|\nabla d|^{2}, we have the following equivalent equation

12​dt−12​d×dt=Δ​d+d​|∇d|2.\frac{1}{2}d_{t}-\frac{1}{2}d\times d_{t}=\Delta d+d|\nabla d|^{2}. (6.1)

Testing (6.1) by dtd_{t} and using (a×b)⋅b=0(a\times b)\cdot b=0 and d⋅dt=0d\cdot d_{t}=0, we get

dd​t​∫Ω|∇d|2​𝑑x+∫Ω|dt|2​𝑑x≤0.\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}|\nabla d|^{2}dx+\int_{\Omega}|d_{t}|^{2}dx\leq 0. (6.2)

Testing (1.23) by −Δ​dt-\Delta d_{t} and using |d|=1|d|=1, we find that

12dd​t∫Ω|Δd|2dx+∫Ω|∇dt|2dx=−∫Ω(d|∇d|2+d×Δd)⋅Δdtdx\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}|\Delta d|^{2}dx+\int_{\Omega}|\nabla d_{t}|^{2}dx=-\int_{\Omega}(d|\nabla d|^{2}+d\times\Delta d)\cdot\Delta d_{t}dx (6.3)
=\displaystyle= ∫Ω∇(d​|∇d|2+d×Δ​d)⋅∇dt​𝑑x\displaystyle\int_{\Omega}\nabla(d|\nabla d|^{2}+d\times\Delta d)\cdot\nabla d_{t}dx
≤\displaystyle\leq C(∥∇d∥Lq∥∇d∥L4​qq−22+∥∇d∥Lq∥Δd∥L2​qq−2+∥∇Δd∥L2)∥∇dt∥L2\displaystyle C(\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}\|\nabla d\|_{L^{\frac{4q}{q-2}}}^{2}+\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{\frac{2q}{q-2}}}+\|\nabla\Delta d\|_{L^{2}})\|\nabla d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}
≤\displaystyle\leq C(∥∇d∥Lq∥Δd∥L2​qq−2+∥∇Δd∥L2)∥∇dt∥L2\displaystyle C(\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{\frac{2q}{q-2}}}+\|\nabla\Delta d\|_{L^{2}})\|\nabla d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}
≤\displaystyle\leq C⁡(‖∇d‖Lq​‖Δ​d‖L21−3q​‖d‖H33q+‖d‖H3)​‖∇dt‖L2\displaystyle C(\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{2}}^{1-\frac{3}{q}}\|d\|_{H^{3}}^{\frac{3}{q}}+\|d\|_{H^{3}})\|\nabla d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}
≤\displaystyle\leq 14​‖∇dt‖L22+δ​‖d‖H32+C​‖∇d‖Lq2​qq−3​‖Δ​d‖L22\displaystyle\frac{1}{4}\|\nabla d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\delta\|d\|_{H^{3}}^{2}+C\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}^{\frac{2q}{q-3}}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{2}}^{2}

for any 0<δ<10<\delta<1. Here we have used the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequalities:

‖∇d‖L4​qq−22≤C​‖d‖L∞​‖Δ​d‖L2​qq−2,\displaystyle\|\nabla d\|_{L^{\frac{4q}{q-2}}}^{2}\leq C\|d\|_{L^{\infty}}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{\frac{2q}{q-2}}}, (6.4)
‖Δ​d‖L2​qq−2≤C​‖Δ​d‖L21−3q​‖d‖H33q.\displaystyle\|\Delta d\|_{L^{\frac{2q}{q-2}}}\leq C\|\Delta d\|_{L^{2}}^{1-\frac{3}{q}}\|d\|_{H^{3}}^{\frac{3}{q}}. (6.5)

Applying ∂i\partial_{i} to (1.23), we get

∂idt−Δ∂id=∂i(d|∇d|2)+∂id×Δd+d×Δ∂id.\partial_{i}d_{t}-\Delta\partial_{i}d=\partial_{i}(d|\nabla d|^{2})+\partial_{i}d\times\Delta d+d\times\Delta\partial_{i}d.

Testing the above equation by Δ​∂id\Delta\partial_{i}d, summing over ii, and using (6.4) and (6.5) and |d|=1|d|=1, we obtain

‖d‖H3\displaystyle\|d\|_{H^{3}} ≤\displaystyle\leq C(∥d∥L2+∥∇Δd∥L2)\displaystyle C(\|d\|_{L^{2}}+\|\nabla\Delta d\|_{L^{2}})
≤\displaystyle\leq C+C​‖∇dt‖L2+C​‖∇(d​|∇d|2)‖L2+∑iC​‖∂id×Δ​d‖L2\displaystyle C+C\|\nabla d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}+C\|\nabla(d|\nabla d|^{2})\|_{L^{2}}+\sum\limits_{i}C\|\partial_{i}d\times\Delta d\|_{L^{2}}
≤\displaystyle\leq C+C​‖∇dt‖L2+C​‖∇d‖Lq​‖∇d‖L4​qq−22+C​‖∇d‖Lq​‖Δ​d‖L2​qq−2\displaystyle C+C\|\nabla d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}+C\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}\|\nabla d\|_{L^{\frac{4q}{q-2}}}^{2}+C\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{\frac{2q}{q-2}}}
≤\displaystyle\leq C+C​‖∇dt‖L2+C​‖∇d‖Lq​‖Δ​d‖L2​qq−2\displaystyle C+C\|\nabla d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}+C\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{\frac{2q}{q-2}}}
≤\displaystyle\leq C+C​‖∇dt‖L2+C​‖∇d‖Lq​‖Δ​d‖L21−3q​‖d‖H33q,\displaystyle C+C\|\nabla d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}+C\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{2}}^{1-\frac{3}{q}}\|d\|_{H^{3}}^{\frac{3}{q}},

which yields

‖d‖H3≤C+C​‖∇dt‖L2+C​‖∇d‖Lqqq−3​‖Δ​d‖L2.\|d\|_{H^{3}}\leq C+C\|\nabla d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}+C\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}^{\frac{q}{q-3}}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{2}}. (6.6)

Plugging (6.6) into (6.3) and taking δ\delta small enough, we have

dd​t​∫Ω|Δ​d|2​𝑑x+∫Ω|∇dt|2​𝑑x\displaystyle\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}|\Delta d|^{2}dx+\int_{\Omega}|\nabla d_{t}|^{2}dx
≤\displaystyle\leq C+C​‖∇d‖Lq2​qq−3​‖Δ​d‖L22\displaystyle C+C\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}^{\frac{2q}{q-3}}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{2}}^{2}
≤\displaystyle\leq C+C​‖∇d‖Lq2​qq−31+log⁡(e+‖∇d‖Lq)​‖Δ​d‖L22​log⁡(e+‖∇d‖Lq)\displaystyle C+C\frac{\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}^{\frac{2q}{q-3}}}{1+\log(e+\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}})}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\log(e+\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}})
≤\displaystyle\leq C+C​‖∇d‖Lq2​qq−31+log⁡(e+‖∇d‖Lq)​‖Δ​d‖L22​log⁡(e+y),\displaystyle C+C\frac{\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}^{\frac{2q}{q-3}}}{1+\log(e+\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}})}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\log(e+y),

which implies

∫Ω|Δ​d|2​𝑑x+∫t0t∫Ω|∇dt|2​𝑑x​𝑑τ≤C​(e+y)C0​ϵ.\int_{\Omega}|\Delta d|^{2}dx+\int_{t_{0}}^{t}\int_{\Omega}|\nabla d_{t}|^{2}dxd\tau\leq C(e+y)^{C_{0}\epsilon}. (6.7)

Provided that

∫t0T‖∇d‖Lq2​qq−31+log⁡(e+‖∇d‖Lq)​𝑑τ≤ϵ<<1,\int_{t_{0}}^{T}\frac{\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}}^{\frac{2q}{q-3}}}{1+\log(e+\|\nabla d\|_{L^{q}})}d\tau\leq\epsilon<<1,

with y⁡(t):=sup[t0,t]‖d‖H3y(t):=\sup\limits_{[t_{0},t]}\|d\|_{H^{3}} for any 0<t0≤t≤T0<t_{0}\leq t\leq T and C0C_{0} is an absolute constant.

It follows from (1.23), (6.6) and (6.7) that

∫Ω|dt|2​𝑑x+∫t0t‖d‖H32​𝑑τ≤C​(e+y)C0​ϵ.\int_{\Omega}|d_{t}|^{2}dx+\int_{t_{0}}^{t}\|d\|_{H^{3}}^{2}d\tau\leq C(e+y)^{C_{0}\epsilon}. (6.8)

Applying ∂t\partial_{t} to (1.23), testing by −Δ​dt-\Delta d_{t}, and using |d|=1|d|=1, (6.7) and (6.8), we have

12dd​t∫Ω|∇dt|2dx+∫Ω|Δdt|2dx=−∫Ω[∂t(d|∇d|2)+dt×Δd]Δdtdx\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}|\nabla d_{t}|^{2}dx+\int_{\Omega}|\Delta d_{t}|^{2}dx=-\int_{\Omega}[\partial_{t}(d|\nabla d|^{2})+d_{t}\times\Delta d]\Delta d_{t}dx
≤\displaystyle\leq C⁡(‖∇d‖L62​‖dt‖L6+‖∇d‖L6​‖∇dt‖L3+‖dt‖L∞​‖Δ​d‖L2)​‖Δ​dt‖L2\displaystyle C(\|\nabla d\|_{L^{6}}^{2}\|d_{t}\|_{L^{6}}+\|\nabla d\|_{L^{6}}\|\nabla d_{t}\|_{L^{3}}+\|d_{t}\|_{L^{\infty}}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{2}})\|\Delta d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}
≤\displaystyle\leq C⁡(‖∇d‖L62​‖dt‖L6+‖Δ​d‖L2​‖∇dt‖L212​‖Δ​dt‖L212+‖Δ​d‖L2​‖dt‖L2)​‖Δ​dt‖L2\displaystyle C(\|\nabla d\|_{L^{6}}^{2}\|d_{t}\|_{L^{6}}+\|\Delta d\|_{L^{2}}\|\nabla d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\|\Delta d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}+\|\Delta d\|_{L^{2}}\|d_{t}\|_{L^{2}})\|\Delta d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}
≤\displaystyle\leq 12​‖Δ​dt‖L22+C​‖d‖H24​‖dt‖H12+C​‖d‖H22​‖dt‖L22,\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\|\Delta d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+C\|d\|_{H^{2}}^{4}\|d_{t}\|_{H^{1}}^{2}+C\|d\|_{H^{2}}^{2}\|d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}^{2},

which implies

∫Ω|∇dt|2​𝑑x+∫t0t‖Δ​dt‖L22​𝑑τ≤C​(e+y)C0​ϵ.\int_{\Omega}|\nabla d_{t}|^{2}dx+\int_{t_{0}}^{t}\|\Delta d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}^{2}d\tau\leq C(e+y)^{C_{0}\epsilon}. (6.9)

It follows from (6.6), (6.7), (6.8) and (6.9) that

‖d‖H3≤C+C​‖∇dt‖L2+C​‖∇d‖L62​‖Δ​d‖L2≤C​(e+y)C0​ϵ,\|d\|_{H^{3}}\leq C+C\|\nabla d_{t}\|_{L^{2}}+C\|\nabla d\|_{L^{6}}^{2}\|\Delta d\|_{L^{2}}\leq C(e+y)^{C_{0}\epsilon},

which leads to

‖d‖L∞​(0,T,H3)≤C.\|d\|_{L^{\infty}(0,T;H^{3})}\leq C.

This completes the proof of Theorem 1.4.

□\square
